python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Data for Jan, Feb, Mar 1941 (in thousands of tons) - from first table
grand_total = [1825, 1801, 2032]
american = [468, 489, 553]

# Calculate percentage for each month
percentages = []
for i in range(3):
    pct = (american[i] / grand_total[i]) * 100
    percentages.append(pct)
    print(f"Month {i+1}: {american[i]}/{grand_total[i]} = {pct:.4f}%")

# Average percentage (or they might want the combined percentage)
total_american = sum(american)
total_grand = sum(grand_total)
combined_pct = (total_american / total_grand) * 100
print(f"\nCombined: {total_american}/{total_grand} = {combined_pct:.4f}%")

# Now calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
# Using the full series from the table (all months from Sept 1940 to Sept 1941)
# First table data (net registered tonnage):
grand_total_series = [3160, 3079, 2571, 1875, 1825, 1801, 2032, 2662, 3694, 4177, 4791, 4657, 3837]
american_series = [644, 608, 491, 486, 468, 489, 553, 680, 940, 1068, 1041, 930, 825]

# Calculate Pearson correlation
n = len(grand_total_series)
mean_x = sum(grand_total_series) / n
mean_y = sum(american_series) / n

numerator = sum((grand_total_series[i] - mean_x) * (american_series[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n))
denominator_x = math.sqrt(sum((x - mean_x)**2 for x in grand_total_series))
denominator_y = math.sqrt(sum((y - mean_y)**2 for y in american_series))

correlation = numerator / (denominator_x * denominator_y)

print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {correlation:.6f}")
print(f"\nResults to output:")
print(f"Percentage (rounded to 1 decimal): {combined_pct:.1f}")
print(f"Correlation (rounded to 3 decimals): {correlation:.3f}")
EOF
